# Wheatstone fidelity certificate calculations

These exact finite tables are the calculation inputs to Theorems E.8.4b.10–11 in [the thermodynamics and area-law section](../../../appendices/appendix_e_thermo_area_law.md). The complete finite source and operation class, complex-frame reduction, weak-duality square identity, polynomial numerators, tensor Bernstein recurrence, fraction-free determinant identities, analytic leaf rules, closed-cover induction and operational normalization remain in those theorems.

The global coordinates are $(u,v,w)$ on the closed root with integer numerator bounds $(0,0,0)$ and $(327680,327680,786432)$ at denominator $786432$. The matrix witnesses are real symmetric $6\times6$ matrices $Z$ and $2\times2$ matrices $\Lambda$ in the theorem's frame. Positive denominators and sparse upper-triangle entries determine every full matrix exactly; reflection supplies the lower triangle, and omitted entries are zero. The matrices $U_p,V_p$ and all polynomial identities used to verify them are explicitly defined by Theorem E.8.4b.11. The separate parallel and antiparallel coefficient tables use their ordered endpoint variables $(u,v)$ and guard numbering of Theorem E.8.4b.10. The rows below preserve every regional interval, closed path, matrix numerator, polynomial coefficient and endpoint reason.

<a id="wheatstone-root-partition"></a>

## Wheatstone closed root partition

**Closed root partition.** All endpoint triples in the first table are integer numerators with common denominator $786432$, in the coordinate order $(u,v,w)$. The root is $[0,327680]\times[0,327680]\times[0,786432]$ at that scale. Remove the initial letter $r$ from a box label to obtain its binary path. At each node, bisect the coordinate with largest side length divided by its corresponding root side length, resolving ties in $(u,v,w)$ order. Bits zero and one select the lower and upper closed children. This determines every box directly, including its faces.

Types $B,A,N,S$ mean constant Bernstein, affine Bernstein, affine normalized Bernstein and affine slack-repaired Bernstein witnesses, respectively. They all use the matrix rule (E.8.4b.11.6); the distinction records which exact rational witness is supplied. Types $C,P,H,R_1,R_2$ denote the central theorem, product-cut theorem, half-mode interval rule, scalar-radius Bernstein rule and spectral-radius Bernstein rule. Their whole-box inequalities are those of part III.

<a id="wheatstone-matrix-witnesses"></a>

## Wheatstone rational matrix witnesses

**Matrix witnesses.** For each matrix leaf let $x_0=1,x_1=u,x_2=v,x_3=w$ and define
$$
Z(u,v,w)=z_d^{-1}\sum_{a=0}^3x_a Z^{(a)},\qquad
\Lambda(u,v,w)=l_d^{-1}\sum_{a=0}^3x_a L^{(a)}.
$$
For a constant witness all positive-degree matrices vanish. Each table entry $(i,j):m$ means the exact integer entry $m$ at position $(i,j)$, indexed from zero. Only upper-triangular nonzero entries are listed; symmetry determines the lower triangle and every omitted entry is zero. The $Z^{(a)}$ are $6\times6$ and the $L^{(a)}$ are $2\times2$. Rows with both matrices zero are omitted. Denominators are positive. The center and radius of a box are respectively $(l+h)/(2\cdot786432)$ and $(h-l)/(2\cdot786432)$, so no extra coordinate data are needed.

**Product-input intervals.** For each row, $[a,b]$ is an interval in the ordered product-input parameter, $\lambda_v,\lambda_w$ are the two positive rational dual parameters and $r_1,\ldots,r_4$ are lower square-root bounds. Let
$$
q=(\lambda_v,\lambda_v/b,\lambda_w,
\lambda_v\lambda_w/[a\lambda_w+(1-a)\lambda_v]),\qquad
r_i=10^{-12}\left\lfloor\sqrt{\lfloor10^{24}q_i\rfloor}\right\rfloor.
$$
Replace each $r_i$ by $\min(6,r_i)$ when evaluating $\phi(r)=2r-r^2/6$. The exact score is $6+2\phi(r_1)+\phi(r_2)+\phi(r_3)+\phi(r_4)-\lambda_v-\lambda_w$. All thirty-six consecutive intervals from $9/25$ to one and every rational score are printed below.

The final trace-only polynomial is printed for completeness and is never used for a guard exclusion. <a id="parallel-endpoint-cut"></a>

## Parallel closed endpoint partition

**Parallel closed endpoint partition.** Starting with $[0,1/2]^2$, alternate $u$ and $v$ midpoint splits, beginning with $u$; bits zero and one choose the lower and upper closed half. Reason zero means that every Bernstein coefficient of the core is nonnegative. A positive reason $k$ means that every coefficient of guard $k$ is strictly negative, excluding the whole box.

<a id="antiparallel-endpoint-cut"></a>

## Antiparallel closed endpoint partition

**Antiparallel closed endpoint partition.** Starting with $[0,1/2]^2$, alternate $u$ and $v$ midpoint splits, beginning with $u$; bits zero and one choose the lower and upper closed half. Reason zero means that every Bernstein coefficient of the core is nonnegative. A positive reason $k$ means that every coefficient of guard $k$ is strictly negative, excluding the whole box.

| Dyadic box word | Reason polynomial |
| --- | --- |
| $0000$ | 1 |
| $0001$ | 3 |
| $0010$ | 2 |
| $0011$ | 0 |
| $010$ | 3 |
| $011000$ | 0 |
| $011001$ | 3 |
| $01101$ | 0 |
| $01110$ | 3 |
| $011110$ | 0 |
| $011111$ | 6 |
| $1000$ | 2 |
| $10010$ | 0 |
| $100110$ | 2 |
| $100111$ | 0 |

| $101100$ | 2 |
| $101101$ | 0 |

| $11110$ | 4 |
| $11111$ | 0 |
